title: TTY canonical input drops bytes outside its printable-ASCII filter
mechanism: In canonical mode LineDiscipline::push_char appends a byte to the current line only when is_printable_char (0x20..0x7e) holds, so bytes such as UTF-8 lead and continuation bytes are silently dropped before the line reaches the read buffer.
contract: termios(3): with ISTRIP clear, canonical input keeps every byte that is not a special editing or line character, so c3 a9 0a written to the master is read back unchanged from the slave.
observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): the slave returns only the newline, and every byte outside 0x20..0x7e that is not a special character is lost from canonical input.

repro.how_to_run: Run `make static` in repro/ on x86-64 Linux, copy bin/abi_probe into an Asterinas guest, and run `abi_probe <case>` for tty_canonical_bytes. repro/README.md gives the saved Linux output.

caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Byte-preservation probe only, not an audit of canonical editing, echo, or erase of multibyte characters. Legacy text-only probe.
